title: Jesse Derry makes first Premier League start for Chelsea
content:
Chelsea have handed a first Premier League start to youngster Jesse Derry against Nottingham Forest.

The 18-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Crystal Palace last summer, has been a regular in Premier League 2 and in the UEFA Youth League this term.

He made his first-team debut in the FA Cup fourth-round tie against Hull City in February and was an unused substitute for the league defeat away at Brighton & Hove Albion last month, Liam Rosenior’s final game in charge.

Derry is the son of Shaun Derry, who made over 600 appearances in English football including Premier League spells at Crystal Palace and Queens Park Rangers.

Callum McFarlane, who replaced Rosenior as head coach until the end of the season, worked with the winger at Under-21 level and has handed him a chance from the start in place of Alejandro Garnacho, who is not part of the matchday squad.

McFarlane watched on Friday night as Derry impressed for the Under-21 side against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League 2 quarter-final. Derry struck the woodwork twice in an impressive display, despite his side’s 3-1 defeat.

Chelsea are without a win in the league since March 4, with Rosenior paying the price for five consecutive defeats.

McFarlane has welcome news with the return to the matchday squad for both Reece James and Levi Colwill, who has not played this season, with both players named on the substitutes’ bench.

McFarlane, who also took charge of two games earlier in the season following the dismissal of Enzo Maresca, won his first game of his second spell with victory over Leeds United in the FA Cup semi-final.

Chelsea sit ninth in the Premier League table, 10 points off the automatic Champions League qualification places, with four games of the season to go.
